raised.claim: `guardHits` is only logged when `covered < orphans.length`, which checks raw LLM output before `planTriageActions` runs, so guard rejections are never logged when the LLM returns a verdict for every orphan.
raised.why_it_breaks: `covered` counts distinct in-batch `beer_id`s present in `analysis.verdicts` (lines 277-279), before `planTriageActions` filters or skips any verdicts. When the LLM obeys the prompt and emits a verdict for all 50 orphans in the batch (`covered === orphans.length`), and Guards 1, 2, 3, or 4 reject or degrade those verdicts, `covered < orphans.length` evaluates to `false` and `guardHits` is silently dropped without logging.

raised.claim: Model-authored `issue.body` is not stripped or sanitized of ` ```triage-scope ` fences before appending `renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)`, allowing the model's prose body to shadow the authoritative scope block.
raised.why_it_breaks: `buildTriagePrompt` shows the model existing open issue bodies, all of which end with a ` ```triage-scope ` block. If the model imitates that format in `new_issues[].body`, `issue.body` will contain a ` ```triage-scope ` block before the appended `renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)`. Because `parseScopeBlock` uses `BLOCK_RE.exec(body)` which matches the first occurrence, subsequent runs will parse the model's prose block instead of the rendered structured `issue.scope`.

raised.claim: Degrading unprobed `not_on_untappd` verdicts to `matcher_bug` in `plan.quiet` causes `orphanTriage` to misreport them as `wontfix` in the daily digest outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: In `src/jobs/orphan-triage.ts` (lines 340-344), the loop over `plan.quiet` does `if (v.review_class === 'not_on_untappd') outcome.notOnUntappd++; else outcome.wontfix++;`. Every `not_on_untappd` verdict degraded by Guard 3 to `review_class: 'matcher_bug'` is pushed to `plan.quiet` and therefore increments `outcome.wontfix`, reporting degraded `matcher_bug` rows as `wontfix` in the digest line and job outcome.

raised.claim: Guard 2 (`rowSatisfiesScope`) is not enforced when attaching verdicts to `new_issues` via `new_issue_key`, and Guard 4 (`postCreationRows >= MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE`) does not count verdicts attached earlier in the same batch.
raised.why_it_breaks:
1) In the `else` branch (`new_issue_key`), a verdict is pushed into `byKey` without checking `rowSatisfiesScope(row, verdict.review_class, newIssue.scope)`, so a model can propose a legal narrow scope for `k1` and attach contradicting rows from the same batch to `k1`.
2) In the `hasIssue` branch, `target.postCreationRows` is static across the loop, so an issue at 11 `postCreationRows` can accept up to 50 additional rows in a single batch before `MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE` (12) trips on the next day's run.

raised.claim: `setEnrichFailureReview` sets `issue_number`, but `recordEnrichFailure` was not updated to clear `issue_number` alongside `review_class`, `review_note`, and `reviewed_at` when `candidates_count` crosses the `0 <-> >0` boundary.
raised.why_it_breaks: When a previously triaged beer fails enrichment again and its `candidates_count` crosses between `0` and `>0`, `recordEnrichFailure` resets `review_class`, `review_note`, and `reviewed_at` to `NULL` so the row re-enters triage, but leaves the old `issue_number` populated on the untriaged row.
